chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from al-Fudayl, who said:
I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, the Exalted:
He said: "It is the obligatory prayer." I said:
"Those who are constant in their salat (prayer)."
He said: "It is the supererogatory prayer."

key_terms.النَّافِلَةُ: the supererogatory prayer, meaning voluntary acts of salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةُ: the obligatory duty, referring to the prescribed salat (prayer)
key_terms.دَائِمُونَ: constant and continuous, understood here as persistence in prayer beyond obligation
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِمْ: their salat (prayer), the act of ritual worship discussed in the verse
key_terms.يُحَافِظُونَ: they carefully preserve and maintain, understood here as guarding the obligatory prayers

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between "maintaining" prayer and being "constant" in prayer in the Quran according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام explains two Quranic descriptions of people devoted to salat (prayer). He interprets maintaining salat (prayer) as referring to the obligatory prayers, and being constant in salat (prayer) as referring to the supererogatory prayers. The narration highlights both the centrality of the prescribed prayers and the added virtue of regular voluntary worship.
